Permanent Driving Licence Application

State / UT: Chandigarh
Date generated: 16 Nov 2026
Verified: 2026-11-14T00:00:00.000Z

Step-by-step procedure to convert your Learner's Licence into a Permanent Driving Licence. Complete document checklist, official government fees (₹700), and driving test rules.

Required Documents Checklist (6 Items)

Original Learner's Licence (LLR)(Mandatory) • Original required for verification

Valid physical or electronic learner licence certificate issued at least 30 days prior.

Application Form 2 Printout(Mandatory) • 1 signed printed copy

Auto-generated completed application form downloaded from Sarathi Parivahan portal.

Fee Payment Receipt and Appointment Slip(Mandatory) • 1 copy

Printed e-receipt confirming government fee payment and booked test slot.

Test Vehicle Documents (RC, Insurance, PUC)(Mandatory) • Original documents for inspection

Valid registration certificate, insurance paper, and pollution certificate for the vehicle brought for testing.

Form 5B Driving School Training Certificate(Conditional) • Original certificate

Certificate from an accredited driving school exempting candidate from physical driving test.

Form 1A Medical Fitness Certificate(Conditional) • Original signed copy

Doctor signed medical certificate mandatory for candidates 40+ years old or commercial categories.

Statutory Fees (Official Gazette Rates)

Fee DescriptionTypeAmount (₹)
Issue of Driving LicenceMandatory₹200
Driving Test Fee (Single Vehicle Class)Mandatory₹300
Smart Card Driving Licence Specification FeeMandatory₹200
Total Mandatory Statutory Fee₹700

* Always demand an official computerized government receipt for every rupee paid. Never pay unreceipted cash.

Procedure Steps (Compact Overview)

  1. 1.
    Complete 30-Day Mandatory Waiting Period[Eligibility Requirement]

    Wait at least 30 days after your Learner's Licence (LLR) was issued. Make sure your LLR has not expired (valid for 180 days).

  2. 2.
    Submit Form 2 Application on Sarathi Parivahan[Official Sarathi Portal (parivahan.gov.in)]

    Visit sarathi.parivahan.gov.in, select your State, and click 'Apply for Driving Licence'. Enter your Learner's Licence number and date of birth to load your details automatically.

  3. 3.
    Select Vehicle Classes & Driving School Certificate[Online Application Form]

    Choose the vehicle classes endorsed on your learner permit (e.g. Motorcycle with Gear - MCWG, Light Motor Vehicle - LMV). If you were trained at an accredited driver training institute (ADTC), upload your Form 5B certificate.

  4. 4.
    Pay Statutory Government Fees Online[Integrated Payment Gateway]

    Pay ₹200 for DL issue, ₹200 for smart card printing, and ₹300 per vehicle class test fee. Total is ₹700 for single class or ₹1,000 for dual class.

  5. 5.
    Book Practical Driving Test Appointment Slot[Sarathi Slot Booking System]

    Select your designated RTO or Automated Driving Test Track (ADTT) and pick an available date and time slot. Download and print the Appointment Slip.

  6. 6.
    Appear for the Practical Driving Test at RTO Track[RTO Driving Test Track / ADTT Center]

    Arrive at the RTO test track 30 minutes before your slot with a vehicle corresponding to your application category. For two-wheelers, demonstrate figure-of-eight (8) balancing and sudden stopping. For four-wheelers, pass the H-track reverse parking, parallel parking, and gradient hill restart without rolling backwards.

  7. 7.
    Test Results and Biometric Data Verification[RTO Biometrics Counter]

    If you pass the test, the testing officer signs your inspection sheet or the automated track sensors submit an instant electronic pass report. Your digital photo and signature are verified.

  8. 8.
    Receive Driving Licence via Speed Post & DigiLocker[Postal Delivery / Digital Download]

    Your permanent driving licence number is generated within 24-48 hours and available on DigiLocker and mParivahan. The physical chip-based Smart Card licence is printed and dispatched to your residential address via India Post Speed Post.

Step-by-Step Procedure

Follow these sequential steps from online registration to final counter collection.

1

Complete 30-Day Mandatory Waiting Period

Eligibility Requirement30 days minimum wait

Wait at least 30 days after your Learner's Licence (LLR) was issued. Make sure your LLR has not expired (valid for 180 days).

2

Submit Form 2 Application on Sarathi Parivahan

Official Sarathi Portal (parivahan.gov.in)10 minutes

Visit sarathi.parivahan.gov.in, select your State, and click 'Apply for Driving Licence'. Enter your Learner's Licence number and date of birth to load your details automatically.

Open Sarathi Driving Licence Application
3

Select Vehicle Classes & Driving School Certificate

Online Application Form5 minutes

Choose the vehicle classes endorsed on your learner permit (e.g. Motorcycle with Gear - MCWG, Light Motor Vehicle - LMV). If you were trained at an accredited driver training institute (ADTC), upload your Form 5B certificate.

Accredited Training School Exemption

Under Section 12 of the Motor Vehicles Act, candidates with a Form 5B certificate from an Accredited Driving School skip the practical RTO driving test.
4

Pay Statutory Government Fees Online

Integrated Payment Gateway5 minutes

Pay ₹200 for DL issue, ₹200 for smart card printing, and ₹300 per vehicle class test fee. Total is ₹700 for single class or ₹1,000 for dual class.

5

Book Practical Driving Test Appointment Slot

Sarathi Slot Booking System5 minutes

Select your designated RTO or Automated Driving Test Track (ADTT) and pick an available date and time slot. Download and print the Appointment Slip.

6

Appear for the Practical Driving Test at RTO Track

RTO Driving Test Track / ADTT Center1-2 hours

Arrive at the RTO test track 30 minutes before your slot with a vehicle corresponding to your application category. For two-wheelers, demonstrate figure-of-eight (8) balancing and sudden stopping. For four-wheelers, pass the H-track reverse parking, parallel parking, and gradient hill restart without rolling backwards.

Bring Vehicle Documents

The vehicle you bring for the test must have valid physical registration certificate (RC), active insurance policy, and valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate.
7

Test Results and Biometric Data Verification

RTO Biometrics Counter15 minutes

If you pass the test, the testing officer signs your inspection sheet or the automated track sensors submit an instant electronic pass report. Your digital photo and signature are verified.

8

Receive Driving Licence via Speed Post & DigiLocker

Postal Delivery / Digital Download7-15 working days for physical card

Your permanent driving licence number is generated within 24-48 hours and available on DigiLocker and mParivahan. The physical chip-based Smart Card licence is printed and dispatched to your residential address via India Post Speed Post.

Immediate Digital Legality

Once your DL number is generated, your digital driving licence in DigiLocker or mParivahan is legally valid across India under CMVR Rule 139.

What to Do After Submission: Status Tracking & Collection

Once you submit your application and biometric verification is complete:

  • Keep the Acknowledgement Slip: Safely note your Application Number or SMS reference to track status on the official portal.
  • Delivery via Speed Post: Physical cards or renewed booklets are dispatched to your registered address via India Post Speed Post with tracking.
  • Digital Download (DigiLocker / mParivahan): Legally valid digital documents become available on DigiLocker immediately upon counter approval under IT Act Rule 9A.

Why Applications Get Rejected

Review these top 3 counter rejection triggers before visiting the office.

Common Mistakes

Applying Before 30-Day Mandatory Waiting Period

Rejection Risk #1

Attempting to book a permanent DL test slot when less than 30 days have elapsed since the learner licence was approved.

How to avoid: Wait until day 31 from the date printed on your Learner Licence Form 3 before scheduling.

Expired Test Vehicle Documentation

Rejection Risk #2

Bringing a vehicle to the test track with expired third-party insurance or expired PUC certificate leads to immediate test cancellation.

How to avoid: Check mParivahan on your phone to verify the vehicle's fitness, insurance, and PUC are active before visiting the track.

Failure on Automated Sensor Tracks (Touching Yellow Lines)

Rejection Risk #3

Automated sensor tracks register a fail if vehicle tyres cross boundary lines or exceed allowed forward-reverse maneuvers.

How to avoid: Practice parallel parking and reverse H-parking beforehand without crossing side curbs.

Frequently Asked Questions

Common citizen doubts answered according to official Ministry circulars.

4 Answers

You can apply exactly 30 days after the date your learner licence was issued. You have up to 180 days (6 months) from the LL issuance date to pass the driving test and obtain your permanent licence.

If you fail the test, you can re-appear for a re-test after a mandatory 7-day practice period. You will need to log into Sarathi Parivahan, pay a re-test fee of ₹300, and book a new appointment slot.

Yes! You can bring either a manual or an automatic transmission vehicle for your test. However, you must arrange the vehicle yourself; RTOs do not provide test vehicles.

For private vehicles, a driving licence is valid for 20 years or until age 40, whichever is earlier. For ages 40 to 50, it is valid for 10 years. For ages 50 to 55, it is valid until age 60. Above age 55, it is renewed every 5 years.

Before You Leave Home

Verify these 5 essential physical items before walking out your door in Chandigarh.

Check #1

All Original Documents

Carry physical originals of all proof papers (Aadhaar, proof of address, birth date proof) for live verification at the counter for Permanent Driving Licence Application.

Check #2

2 Sets of Self-Attested Photocopies

Black-and-white photocopies signed with your signature and today's date in blue or black ink across the blank margin.

Check #3

Passport Photographs

2 to 4 recent passport photos (35mm x 45mm, plain white background, front-facing without tinted glasses).

Check #4

Accepted Payment Mode

UPI app or active debit card for statutory portal fees, plus ₹200–₹500 exact cash change if counter fees apply.

Check #5

Appointment Slip & SMS

Physical printout of your appointment booking acknowledgment receipt & application reference number (ARN).
